parsed.why: Adds broad care bans, prison-care denial and surgical document rules to hostile national entry/facility regime; only partial recourse via gender-identity hate-crime coverage, no non-discrimination law.
Documented statewide public-accommodation and hate-crime protections, self-declared markers and a care shield materially offset the national regime; unenforced sodomy law is tangential.
No current facility ban and the 2016 bathroom law was repealed, but no statewide gender-identity protections or hate-crime recourse and narrowing document rules leave it near the parent line.

Explicit 2025 facility ban with a private cause of action is a universal-exposure measure; no state hate-crime or nondiscrimination protection and hostile document/care rules compound the national regime.

Working nondiscrimination, hate-crime enforcement and panic-defence repeal are real positives, but recent care/sports bans and restrictive birth-certificate rules keep it below the strongest protective tier.
